item.title: Rust Lifetimes
item.description: A lifetime annotation 'a does not make a value live longer. It is a contract stating which input a returned reference borrows from, and the borrow checker combines that contract with each reference’s last use to compute borrow regions. The first post in a Rust study series.

item.title: Rust Ownership and Freeing Memory
item.description: Rust has no garbage collector. Every value has a single owner, and the value is dropped where that owner’s scope ends. Because the drop point is fixed by scopes in the source code, files and locks are cleaned up by the same rule as memory. The first post in a Rust study series.

item.title: Why Put a Rust Sidecar Next to a Go Service
item.description: A Rust sidecar next to a Go service is a latency-budget decision, not a language preference. Moving pointer-heavy, long-lived data off the Go heap cuts GC cost, and running it as a process in the same Pod avoids a network hop. Covers GC diagnosis, the costs, and when the setup fits.

item.title: quant-investment-platform — mid-retrospective
item.description: A mid-project retrospective on a personal automated trading platform built with Rust + Python + React. With ETF rebalancing and single-stock signal trading both in place, a record of how the safety layers — halt, block, detect, simulate — got built before going live.

item.title: rust-server
item.description: A record of implementing the multithreaded HTTP server from Rust Book Chapter 20, experiencing how ownership and concurrency safety are enforced at the type level.
